reader.requirement: At --std 85 one OPEN statement must accept file-names of mixed organization and access mode, in any mix of INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND groups, with per-file phrases screened against each file's own module, and execute as separate OPEN statements in written order (a failing file does not stop the later ones).

edition-consulted.switches: the OPEN SHARING phrase requires 2002; refused at 85 (COBOL0900)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the mixed-organization permission is the same; the editions differ only in REVERSED and SHARING
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf23_02 covers one mixed OPEN; a failed open inside a mixed list, OPTIONAL relative input, and the per-module phrase refusals are not exercised

probes.printed: OPEN OUTPUT SQ RL IX IR -> 00000000; OPEN I-O IX IR INPUT RL MS -> 00 00 00 05 and reads succeed; OPEN INPUT RL NX IX with NX missing -> USE fires with 35, RL 00, IX 00 and IX then reads K1CC
probes.expected: GR24: as separate OPEN statements in order; optional missing input 05; a missing non-optional file 35 without affecting the others

probes.printed: COBOL2210 OPEN 'RL' REVERSED; n_open_norewind_idx.cob COBOL1802 IX WITH NO REWIND; n_open_extend_linage.cob COBOL2372 EXTEND on a LINAGE file
probes.expected: §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR1 and SR3 and the relative/indexed formats

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the OPEN SHARING phrase requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: SHARING is not in the 1985 format

probes.printed: exit 0: OPEN INPUT SQ REVERSED RL IX OUTPUT LP SQ WITH NO REWIND I-O IX RL EXTEND SQ accepted
probes.expected: REVERSED is a 1985 phrase for sequential files; groups of every mode may mix organizations

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR4  (4.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4
OK  §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR24  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR24

reader.notes: BindOpen screens each file-name against its own organization and emits one implicit OPEN per file, so mixed lists compile and run as separate opens; the edition gates touch only REVERSED and SHARING. The refusal diagnostics cite §2023 clauses at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: o1.cob: OPEN EXTEND SQ RL IX with RL dynamic and IX random refused COBOL2372 for RL and IX only (the relative/indexed module's own rule, per file in the mixed list). o2.cob: an SD file in OPEN OUTPUT SQ SW RL refused COBOL1692. o3.cob (runs/o3-001): RL already open, OPEN OUTPUT SQ RL IX printed 'USE 00 41 99' then 'OPEN-MIX 00 41 00', and WRITE IX and WRITE SQ then succeed 00: the failing middle file does not stop the later one and order holds. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR4 'need not all have the same organization or access'; OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR24 'as if a separate OPEN statement had been written'; OK §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR1 'The EXTEND phrase must only be used for files in the sequential access mode'. The COBOL2372 message cites §2023 at --std 85 (cosmetic, as the reader noted).
